### Required change (to the author, lane `build/M0-a-06-fix-s3` or the session's naming)

* **B-1 (remaining).** Decide a split vertex's on-run test so that it covers every piece the vertex could have split,
  without history. The piece a crossing split when it was created has ends that are still on the stretch before the
  batch: the stretch's own ends, or earlier crossings, which only a removal dissolves. One reading that fits C-0223 is
  this. A split vertex v lies on its run when it is within the hot pixel of the segment a–b for SOME a on one side and b
  on the other, where each of a and b is one of the stretch's vertices that the dissolution walks through (as
  `onStretch` walks) or the stretch's end. Checked on the pre-batch arena, that test covers both readings the tree has
  now (a = b's nearest neighbours; a, b = the ends). It also covers 817 (0.62 cm to (1489,2803)–(2834,2004)) and 1526
  (0.64 cm). Accumulated drift is not bounded by a fixed multiple of the hot pixel, so a wider tolerance is not a fix.
  Pin cases 817 and 1526 (`repro-817.mts`; the arenas are in the table above) as fixtures that assert contentPrint,
  chunk refs, records per level and level digests equal to the pre-insert state. Widen the property, or add a second
  one, so that it draws chains that cross one EDGE three or more times (a zigzag across a base, as `probe-double.mts`
  draws). The current property's random 2 – 4-point chains rarely do. If the session prefers the N-45 route instead
  (detect and refuse), a removal that would leave a split crossing undissolved must be refused, not committed.
